Peru: Despite intense heat in Zaña, people say “We are melting with love for Pope Leo XIV”
The Holy Father will carry out his final engagement of the day at the Sanctuary of Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo.
Representatives from more than 60 parishes will also take part in the gathering, including migrants from Venezuela. ANDINA/Andrés Valle
Not even the scorching sun can dampen the joy of the faithful and visitors from various regions in the district of Zaña—located in the Chiclayo province of the Lambayeque region—who, dressed in the colors of the Vatican (white and yellow), wait in eager anticipation to see Pope Leo XIV and receive his blessing.
Published: 11/14/2026

Around 5:30 p.m., the Holy Father hold a prayer gathering with the Catholic community to mark the conclusion of the Jubilee Year of Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo, at the sanctuary that bears his name.
Long lines of citizens—both locals and foreigners—have formed to enter the religious site, while those unable to get inside have gathered along the perimeter.
Entire families have traveled from other regions, such as Piura, Tumbes, and Lima.
The many colorful umbrellas brought by the eager attendees stand out. The "feels-like" temperature exceeds 34 degrees Celsius (93°F), yet they say... “Melting—but with love for the Pope”
A lovely initiative can also be seen: hand fans featuring an image of the Holy Father. They also contain tourist and cultural information about the Pope’s route, including details on churches, beaches, sanctuaries, and natural sites.
Inside the Sanctuary of Saint Toribio de Mogrovejo, a choir of over 250 members—comprising young men and girls—will perform. The group includes delegations from Cayaltí, Oyotún, Zaña, and Motupe, who have spent more than three months preparing to offer the best possible performance for the Supreme Pontiff.
Representatives from over 60 parishes will also take part in the gathering, including migrants from Venezuela. There is a heavy security presence provided by the police and the military.
Zaña—located an hour away from Chiclayo—is a town of faith. More than four centuries ago, Saint Toribio de Mogrovejo arrived in these lands on a pastoral mission and eventually passed away there.
Today marks the 300th anniversary of his canonization. Pope Leo XIV [sic] is heading to Zaña amidst the great excitement of the people of Chiclayo.

Chennai: A weather system over the southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday evening, with the forecast indicating a possible crossing of the north Tamil Nadu coast.
Storm warning signal Number 1 has been hoisted at nine ports as a precaution. The low-pressure area has strengthened into a well-marked low-pressure area, and is expected to move northwestwards, concentrating into a depression over the same region on Sunday, as per the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
It is subsequently likely to move north-northwestwards and strengthen further. By Monday evening, the system is expected to develop into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south Bay of Bengal and the adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal.
The forecast points to the storm moving towards the north Tamil Nadu coast. However, the information provided does not specify the precise location or timing of a possible landfall, or the wind speeds expected when the system approaches the coast.
Fishermen have been advised against venturing into the deep sea in view of the developing weather system. They have also been instructed to anchor their boats securely along the shore as a precaution against potentially adverse conditions.
The advisory places particular emphasis on keeping fishing vessels safe while the system strengthens over the Bay of Bengal. Its projected intensification over the next two days has prompted warnings for fishing activity and precautionary signals at ports.
The ports named in the warning include Chennai, Cuddalore, Nagapattinam, Rameswaram and Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu, besides Puducherry and Karaikal. Although the report states that signals have been raised at nine ports, it identifies only these seven locations.
The warning comes as the system progresses through successive stages of development, from a low-pressure area to a well-marked low-pressure area, with further strengthening into a depression and then a cyclonic storm anticipated.
The immediate concern is the safety of fishermen and their boats ahead of the expected intensification. The advice to avoid the deep sea and secure vessels remains the principal precaution outlined in the report.
–IANS
